headword: {伝統芸能|でんとうげいのう}

definitions.explanation: Performing art forms that have been passed down through generations in Japan, including kabuki, noh, bunraku, and traditional dance. Composed of 伝統 (tradition) + 芸能 (performing arts).

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{伝統芸能|でんとうげいのう}を{鑑賞|かんしょう}した。
examples.english: I watched a traditional Japanese performing art.

examples.japanese: {歌舞伎|かぶき}は{日本|にほん}を{代表|だいひょう}する{伝統芸能|でんとうげいのう}だ。
examples.english: Kabuki is a representative traditional performing art of Japan.

examples.japanese: {伝統芸能|でんとうげいのう}の{後継者|こうけいしゃ}{不足|ぶそく}が{深刻|しんこく}な{問題|もんだい}になっている。
examples.english: The shortage of successors for traditional performing arts has become a serious problem.

notes:
USAGE:
{伝統芸能|でんとうげいのう} encompasses a wide range of Japanese performing arts with long histories. Major forms include {能|のう} (noh), {歌舞伎|かぶき} (kabuki), {文楽|ぶんらく} (bunraku puppet theater), {狂言|きょうげん} (kyogen comedy), and {日本舞踊|にほんぶよう} (Japanese classical dance).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {伝統芸能|でんとうげいのう}を{鑑賞|かんしょう}する (to watch traditional performing arts)
- {伝統芸能|でんとうげいのう}を{継承|けいしょう}する (to inherit/carry on traditional arts)
- {伝統芸能|でんとうげいのう}の{後継者|こうけいしゃ} (successor of traditional arts)
